neighbours.label: equity jurisprudence: 'equity' as a body of law and its institutions (court of equity, Chancery, equitable remedies)
fire: A plaintiff who comes to a court of equity must have acted fairly himself.
The dispute over the will was sent to the Court of Chancery.
Rescission is an equitable remedy that undoes the contract.
Under the old system, a suit in equity could take decades to resolve.
The judge refused equitable relief because the buyer had delayed too long.
Trusts were first enforced by the Chancellor sitting in Chancery.
Courts of equity would order specific performance where money was not enough.
The maxims of equity say that delay defeats a claim.
quiet: A plaintiff who comes to a criminal court must be represented by counsel.
The dispute over the will was sent to the county court.
Damages are a legal payment that compensates for the breach.
Under the old system, a suit for debt could take years to resolve.
The judge refused bail because the accused had fled before.
Trusts are often set up by parents for their children's education.
The shareholders hold most of the company's equity after the merger.
Homeowners can borrow against the equity in their property.
